description.narrative: The Project will increase consumer access to dairy and juice beverage products and therefore contribute to food security and nutrition in Guinea where prevalence of undernutrition, stunting and wasting is high. Protein intake per capita and day is also low. IFC expects the Project will increase value addition and create jobs. IFCs analysis of the Project suggests average multiplier effects on the value-added dimension, with an overall value addition estimated at US$3,5million, including 150 direct jobs and 300 indirect and induced jobs along the Projects supply chain. The investment, complemented by IFC Advisory, will increase competitiveness in the market supporting (i) local dairy processing to gradually substitute imports; (ii) expansion of canned juice production line; and (iii) technical and operations improvements in terms of adoption of plant and food safety standards of a leading player in Guineas dairy and fruit juice industry, with demonstration and replication potential.

The proposed investment is a debt package which consists of an IFC A loan of up to EUR5.6 million and a Blended Finance (BF) senior loan of up to EUR5.6 million (the IFC Loan) to support the expansion and diversification program of Société Lierkang Diaguissa en Guinee SARL (the Company or Solidiagui), one of the leading fruit juice companies in Guinea-Conakry. IFC would finance the (i) expansion of the current juice beverage production capacity and (ii) installation of a dairy products line within the existing production hall to produce yoghurt and liquid milk (the Project). Solidiagui has been distributing beverage brands including Sagiko juice and Incolac milk products since 2009, then started manufacturing its own brand Fruitalos and Sagiko juice under license upon completion of its factory in 2021 .
